prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1304; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the policyholder's driver regarding a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Claimant reports neck and head pain and states they were struck while stopped at a red light. Claimant is unrepresented and was given the standard claims packet.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Police report obtained, which lists the claimant as a passenger-side occupant of the vehicle that was struck from behind.

Entry 3: Statements taken from two independent witnesses and the other driver. All three describe the impact the same way the claimant did. Scene photos received and reviewed; rear bumper and trunk damage appears consistent with the reported force of impact.

Entry 4: Claimant was diagnosed with a concussion at urgent care the day after the collision. The diagnosis is reasonable for a collision of this type. Medical records show no prior injury to the head or neck area on file.

Entry 5: Claimant added a few smaller details in a follow-up call, such as the exact position of the other car before impact. The core account has not changed from the first report. Vehicle history checked; no prior damage claims on record.

Entry 6: A neighbor mentioned seeing the vehicle with body damage several weeks before the stated loss date. This is an unverified recollection and is being noted for follow-up. Treatment has followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant improved; the file remains open pending the final medical update.
